title: Character & Conduct
description: Little Muslim → Mid. Short questions for children who know the first character basics. Covers commitments, practicing good advice, checking reports, admitting uncertainty, avoiding baseless suspicion, backbiting and false accusation, accepting correction, truthful reporting, honest measures, anger, gentleness, useful effort, different ages, neighbors, companionship, parents, fairness toward children, modest giving, friendly welcomes and ordinary confidence. Uses familiar classroom, play and family situations. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar words. All questions are Mid level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Builds on first manners through familiar meanings, simple distinctions and straightforward daily applications. No specialist legal terms, detailed exception lists, narrator biographies or memorization of reference numbers is required. Level is editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith reports checked during preparation. The Sunan Abi Dawud 4943 report is graded Sahih by Al-Albani on the linked source; the other hadith reports are from Sahih al-Bukhari or Sahih Muslim. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Present-day situations illustrate applications; they are not events narrated in the cited reports. Commitments concern suitable, harmless actions, not promises to conceal harm or do wrong. Changing circumstances are addressed through honest communication rather than a claim that every inability to fulfill a promise is deliberate wrongdoing. The distinction between words and actions encourages improvement rather than labeling children hypocrites. Verification and honest uncertainty do not require a child to investigate danger personally or prove a concern before telling a trusted adult. The verse about an unreliable reporter is not used to label a particular classmate an evildoer. Avoiding suspicion is not an instruction to ignore warning signs. Backbiting and false accusation are distinguished without treating every truthful disclosure as forbidden; appropriate reporting for help is different from malicious gossip. The arrogance report is used to teach accepting truth, not to judge a child's faith, final destiny, clothing or disability. Justice examples use accurate reports to a teacher and simple classroom exchanges, not adult court duties. Anger is distinguished from harmful behavior; children are not required to suppress every feeling or accept mistreatment. Gentleness allows safe boundaries. Useful effort and seeking Allah's help are taught without judging health, physical strength or access to support. Respect for elders and parents is not unconditional obedience to harmful demands; younger children retain dignity and safety. Food sharing requires suitable adult arrangements. The companionship comparison concerns influence, not the worth of craftspeople or a person's smell, income or clothing. Fairness toward children is taught without deciding detailed gift-distribution rulings or asking children to judge their families. Small giving requires suitable permission and is not a demand to give away necessities. Friendly welcomes do not require a child to smile constantly or disregard distress. The confidence example follows Anas's report, but does not tell a child to hide abuse, threats or unsafe secrets from a trusted adult. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach about the commitments we make?

options.text: Take them seriously and fulfill them
Forget them as soon as convenient
Make them only to impress people
Treat other people's trust as a game

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches honoring commitments. In daily life, make suitable promises carefully and try to keep them.

questions.question: What mismatch does the Quran warn believers about?

options.text: Learning before giving advice
Saying good things we do not practice
Admitting that we need to improve
Trying to put a lesson into practice

questions.explanation: The verses warn against saying what we do not do. Good advice should encourage us to improve our own actions too.

questions.question: Why does the Quran teach checking unreliable news?

options.text: To make rumors more exciting
To find a quicker way to blame someone
To avoid harming people through ignorance
To collect the largest audience

questions.explanation: The verse connects checking news with avoiding harm and regret. Care matters before acting on a damaging report.

questions.question: Which approach fits the Quran's warning about following what we do not know?

options.text: Pretend every guess is a fact
Claim we saw what we did not see
Accuse whoever seems easiest to blame
Admit uncertainty instead of inventing certainty

questions.explanation: The Quran warns against following what we lack knowledge of. Honest limits matter in what we claim to know.

questions.question: Which attitude does the Quran tell believers to be careful about?

options.text: Unfounded suspicion about others
Checking facts fairly
Asking for help with a concern
Accepting a harmless explanation

questions.explanation: The verse warns against many suspicions. We should not turn a guess about someone into an accusation without grounds.

questions.question: Does a hurtful comment about an absent person become acceptable gossip simply because it is true?

options.text: Yes, truth makes every hurtful conversation kind
No, true faults can still be backbiting
Yes, gossip is wrong only if invented
No, because backbiting means giving a compliment

questions.explanation: The hadith distinguishes backbiting from false accusation. A true fault is not automatic permission to spread hurtful talk.

questions.question: Which behavior belongs to arrogance as explained in the hadith?

options.text: Accepting a useful correction
Wearing clean clothes without belittling anyone
Rejecting truth and looking down on people
Asking for help to understand

questions.explanation: The hadith explains arrogance through rejecting truth and contempt for people. Learning includes being willing to accept a correct answer.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach about fairness when the truth goes against ourselves?

options.text: Change the facts to protect our image
Tell the truth only when we win
Blame someone else automatically
Stand for justice even then

questions.explanation: The verse teaches justice even against ourselves or close relatives. Personal advantage should not decide whether we tell the truth.

questions.question: What unfair dealing do the opening verses of Al-Mutaffifin condemn?

options.text: Taking full measure but giving others less
Giving the amount that was agreed
Checking that a measure is accurate
Correcting an accidental short measure

questions.explanation: The verses condemn demanding full measure for ourselves while shortchanging others. Honest dealing respects both sides of an exchange.

questions.question: Which kind of strength does the Prophet ﷺ praise in the hadith about anger?

options.text: Always winning a wrestling match
Controlling ourselves when angry
Frightening smaller children
Breaking something whenever upset

questions.explanation: The hadith praises control during anger. Feeling upset does not require us to hurt someone or damage their belongings.

questions.question: Which quality does the hadith describe as making things better?

options.text: Cruelty
Deliberate humiliation
Gentleness
Needless harshness

questions.explanation: The hadith praises gentleness. A calm, respectful approach can improve how we speak, teach and correct mistakes.

questions.question: Which pair of actions fits the hadith's guidance about seeking benefit?

options.text: Give up immediately and mock effort
Ask for help but refuse every useful action
Work only to humiliate other learners
Make useful efforts and seek Allah's help

questions.explanation: The report encourages seeking what benefits us and asking Allah for help. Effort and reliance on Allah belong together.

questions.question: Which pair of attitudes does the hadith teach toward younger and older people?

options.text: Mercy toward the young and respect for elders
Cruelty toward the young and contempt for elders
Kindness only toward people our own age
Respect only for whoever owns expensive things

questions.explanation: The report teaches care for younger people and recognition of elders' rights. Age differences should encourage consideration rather than cruelty.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ encourage Abu Dharr to do when preparing broth?

options.text: Forget that neighbors exist
Remember his neighbors and share with them
Make sharing depend on a costly feast
Boast that nobody else deserves food

questions.explanation: The report encourages considering neighbors when preparing food. Sharing can be thoughtful without becoming a display of wealth.

questions.question: What lesson does the comparison of good and harmful companions highlight?

options.text: A friend's clothes determine their worth
Only perfume sellers may have friends
The company we keep can influence us
Every person has the same effect on our habits

questions.explanation: The hadith illustrates how companions can affect us. Seek friendships that encourage good conduct rather than pressure us toward harm.

questions.question: How does the Quran teach us to speak to parents, especially in old age?

options.text: Harshly whenever their needs take time
With insults whenever we feel tired
As though their dignity does not matter
Respectfully, without scolding or contempt

questions.explanation: The verse teaches honoring parents and speaking respectfully. Patient words matter, especially when older parents need care.

questions.question: In the report about a father's gift, what did the Prophet ﷺ tell him?

options.text: Be fair to his children
Give only to the child who boasts most
Ignore every child's need for fairness
Use gifts to make siblings hate each other

questions.explanation: The report emphasizes fairness toward children. Family care should not turn into favoritism that treats one child as worthless.

questions.question: What does the encouragement to give even half a date teach?

options.text: Only expensive gifts have value
Even a small charitable gift can matter
People with little must never give
Giving must always impress a crowd

questions.explanation: The report encourages charity even in a small amount. We should not dismiss a suitable gift just because it is modest.

questions.question: Which small good deed does the hadith give as an example?

options.text: Making a newcomer feel unwanted
Laughing at someone who is upset
Meeting another person with a friendly face
Refusing every harmless greeting

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches not dismissing small good deeds. A friendly welcome can be a simple way to show kindness.

questions.question: Which quality does Anas's report about a private matter illustrate?

options.text: Broadcasting every private conversation
Inventing a secret to gain attention
Using private information to embarrass someone
Keeping something entrusted in confidence

questions.explanation: Anas described keeping a matter entrusted to him. Respect ordinary privacy, while always telling a trusted adult about harm or unsafe secrets.

questions.question: Does keeping promises mean making commitments we never intend to keep?

options.text: No, commitments should be sincere and taken seriously
Yes, sounding impressive is enough
Yes, another person's expectations never matter
No, because every harmless promise is forbidden

questions.explanation: Promises should not be tools for misleading people. Make realistic commitments and speak honestly if circumstances prevent you from fulfilling them.

questions.question: If we remind others to be kind, should we also work on our own behavior?

options.text: No, advice removes our need to improve
Yes, try to practice the good we encourage
No, kindness applies only to other people
Yes, but only when someone is watching

questions.explanation: The warning about words and actions calls us to practice what we encourage. Needing improvement is a reason to learn, not pretend.

questions.question: Does a worrying report become proven just because a large group repeats it?

options.text: Yes, crowd size replaces evidence
Yes, repetition makes every accusation true
No, checking still matters
No, because checking is always useless

questions.explanation: The Quran's warning concerns harm caused by acting without proper checking. Popularity alone does not establish whether a damaging claim is true.

questions.question: Is saying "I do not know" better than falsely claiming to have seen an event?

options.text: No, a confident guess is always a fact
No, every question requires an invented answer
Yes, but only if we then blame someone anyway
Yes, honest uncertainty avoids inventing evidence

questions.explanation: Honesty includes recognizing the limits of our knowledge. We should not present something as witnessed when we did not see it.

questions.question: Does a missing item automatically prove that the nearest child took it?

options.text: No, suspicion alone is not proof
Yes, being nearby always proves guilt
Yes, guesses never need checking
No, because missing items must never be reported

questions.explanation: A guess about another person is not established fact. Search calmly and ask a trusted adult for help rather than accusing without grounds.

questions.question: If a fault we mention is not actually present, what does the hadith call that?

options.text: A helpful compliment
A false accusation rather than merely backbiting
Proof that the story is harmless
A required part of every friendship

questions.explanation: The hadith distinguishes a true fault discussed hurtfully from an invented accusation. Neither distinction makes malicious talk a good activity.

questions.question: Does accepting a correct answer from a younger learner make us less valuable?

options.text: Yes, truth matters only from older children
Yes, being corrected always removes our dignity
No, accepting truth is better than rejecting it proudly
No, but we must insult the learner afterward

questions.explanation: Rejecting truth out of pride is part of the hadith's warning. We can learn from someone without treating age as a contest.

questions.question: Does loyalty to a friend make it right to give a false account for them?

options.text: Yes, friendship changes falsehood into truth
Yes, only strangers deserve accurate reports
No, because close friends never make mistakes
No, fairness still requires truthful reporting

questions.explanation: The verse teaches justice even when people close to us are involved. Loyalty is not permission to distort what happened.

questions.question: Is it fair to demand ten items while secretly giving only eight in the same agreed exchange?

options.text: No, both sides should receive the agreed amount
Yes, only our share needs to be correct
Yes, clever counting makes every trick fair
No, because counting is always forbidden

questions.explanation: The Quran condemns shortchanging others while demanding full measure for ourselves. The same concern for honesty applies to a simple exchange.

questions.question: Does controlling anger mean we must never feel upset?

options.text: Yes, any upset feeling makes us worthless
No, it concerns how we act when angry
Yes, we must pretend every hurt feels pleasant
No, because anger always permits hitting

questions.explanation: The hadith praises self-control during anger, not pretending feelings do not exist. We can name our feelings without harming others.

questions.question: Can we correct a mistake firmly while still being gentle?

options.text: No, correction always requires insults
No, gentleness means every wrong must continue
Yes, clear guidance can be respectful
Yes, but only if we embarrass the person first

questions.explanation: Gentleness is compatible with clear limits and useful correction. It does not require ignoring a harmful action or humiliating a learner.

questions.question: Does asking Allah for help mean refusing all useful effort?

options.text: Yes, useful practice is always pointless
Yes, every effort shows a lack of trust
No, because asking Allah is never encouraged
No, seeking benefit and asking Allah go together

questions.explanation: The hadith combines useful effort with seeking Allah's help. It does not make learning, practice or suitable assistance enemies of trust.

questions.question: Does respecting older people mean younger children's feelings and safety do not matter?

options.text: No, the hadith also teaches mercy toward the young
Yes, young children never deserve consideration
Yes, age gives permission for every harmful demand
No, because respect for elders is always wrong

questions.explanation: The report joins care for the young with respect for elders. Neither group should be treated as without dignity or protection.

questions.question: Must a family prepare a luxury feast before showing kindness with shared food?

options.text: Yes, simple food never expresses kindness
No, the report gives an ordinary cooking example
Yes, sharing is only for famous families
No, because every neighbor must receive nothing

questions.explanation: The broth example makes neighborly care familiar and practical. Families can share appropriately without making expense the measure of kindness.

questions.question: Should we judge a friendship only by how expensive the other child's belongings are?

options.text: Yes, costly belongings guarantee good character
Yes, kindness has no place in choosing company
No, their influence on conduct matters more
No, because every friendship must be avoided

questions.explanation: The comparison concerns a companion's influence. Wealth and fashionable belongings do not guarantee that a friendship encourages good choices.

questions.question: Does feeling tired give us permission to speak contemptuously to an elderly parent?

options.text: Yes, tiredness makes every insult kind
Yes, older people have no dignity
No, because a parent may never need help
No, respectful speech still matters

questions.explanation: The verse teaches respectful words rather than scolding. We can explain our limits politely and seek suitable help when needed.

questions.question: Does being the youngest mean a child's need for fair treatment can be ignored?

options.text: No, children should be treated fairly
Yes, only the oldest child deserves fairness
Yes, younger children have no feelings
No, because gifts always replace respectful behavior

questions.explanation: The report emphasizes justice toward children. Being younger does not make someone less deserving of consideration within the family.

questions.question: Should we dismiss a suitable charitable gift only because it is small?

options.text: Yes, only a costly gift matters
No, modest giving can still be valuable
Yes, every small gift is an insult
No, because children must give everything they own

questions.explanation: The encouragement to give even a small amount opposes belittling modest charity. Giving should remain suitable and follow necessary adult guidance.

questions.question: Does every kind act require buying something?

options.text: Yes, kindness always needs a purchase
Yes, only costly greetings have value
No, a friendly welcome can be kind too
No, because welcoming people has no value

questions.explanation: The hadith includes a friendly face among small good deeds. Kindness has forms beyond spending money.

questions.question: Does respecting a private confidence mean hiding harm from trusted adults?

options.text: Yes, every secret must be kept even if dangerous
Yes, asking for protection is always betrayal
No, because every private detail belongs online
No, unsafe secrets should be shared with a trusted adult

questions.explanation: Respect for ordinary confidence is different from concealing harm. A child should always seek help about unsafe situations or frightening demands for secrecy.

questions.question: You promised to bring a shared project tomorrow but become ill. What is a responsible next step?

options.text: Ask an adult to help explain and arrange a solution
Pretend you never made the promise
Blame the class without explanation
Make more promises you cannot keep

questions.explanation: Taking commitments seriously includes honest communication when circumstances change. Seek help rather than misleading people who are relying on you.

questions.question: You tell classmates to keep the reading corner tidy. What should you also do?

options.text: Leave your own books scattered deliberately
Put your own materials away
Say that the rule never applies to you
Mock anyone who notices your mess

questions.explanation: Let your actions support the good advice you give. The verse's warning encourages sincerity rather than empty instructions to others.

questions.question: An unchecked message says a classmate damaged school property. What is a careful response?

options.text: Forward it with an angry accusation
Add guessed details
Ask a teacher to check before spreading blame
Treat every forwarded message as proven

questions.explanation: The verse warns about harm from unchecked news. An adult can help establish facts without turning a rumor into public blame.

questions.question: A teacher asks who broke a ruler, but you did not see it happen. What should you say?

options.text: I saw it, though I actually did not
It must be the child I dislike
My guess is proof enough
I did not see who did it

questions.explanation: Say what you actually know. Honest uncertainty helps avoid false claims and unfair blame.

questions.question: Your pencil is missing and a new child sits nearby. What should you avoid?

options.text: Accusing the child merely because they are nearby
Checking your own pencil case
Asking the teacher for help
Looking calmly where you last used it

questions.explanation: The warning about suspicion discourages baseless accusations. A missing pencil does not make a nearby child guilty.

questions.question: Friends mock an absent child's real mistake and say, "But it is true." What reminder fits?

options.text: Every true mistake must be shared for amusement
Truth alone does not make hurtful gossip acceptable
A real fault gives unlimited permission to ridicule
Only invented insults can ever be wrong

questions.explanation: The hadith explains that backbiting can concern a real fault. Reporting a problem to get appropriate adult help is different from mocking someone.

questions.question: A younger classmate correctly notices an error in your answer. What is a humble response?

options.text: Reject it only because they are younger
Insist your age changes the facts
Accept the correction and thank them
Insult them for helping

questions.explanation: The warning about arrogance includes rejecting truth. A useful correction is an opportunity to learn rather than a reason to belittle someone.

questions.question: You saw your friend break a classroom rule. A teacher asks what happened. What is fair?

options.text: Change the story to protect your friend
Accuse an uninvolved child
Invent details to make your friend seem perfect
Describe honestly what you actually saw

questions.explanation: Justice includes truthful reporting when friends are involved. Speak accurately to the teacher instead of spreading the incident around.

questions.question: In a pretend shop, you agree to give ten counters but quietly hand over eight. What should you correct?

options.text: Give the agreed ten rather than shortchanging the buyer
Demand extra counters for your trick
Claim eight and ten are always equal
Hide the missing amount to win

questions.explanation: This classroom example applies the lesson of honest measure. Correct the amount instead of taking advantage of the other person.

questions.question: You lose a game and feel like throwing someone else's pieces. Which choice shows the praised strength?

options.text: Throw them to prove your strength
Pause and keep yourself from damaging them
Threaten the smallest player
Blame anger as permission for destruction

questions.explanation: The hadith praises control when angry. You can step back and ask for help while keeping people and belongings safe.

questions.question: A younger learner keeps mixing up two words. Which correction shows gentleness?

options.text: Call them worthless
Make the class laugh at them
Explain patiently and let them try again
Say they never deserve help

questions.explanation: Gentleness can make correction more helpful. Patient explanation supports learning without turning a mistake into humiliation.

questions.question: You find a lesson difficult. Which plan combines useful effort with seeking Allah's help?

options.text: Refuse all practice and demand instant success
Mock everyone who studies
Treat one mistake as a reason to stop forever
Ask Allah for help, practice and ask your teacher

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages beneficial effort and seeking Allah's help. A manageable practice plan and teacher support are useful ways to keep learning.

questions.question: You join a family activity with a younger cousin and a grandparent. Which attitude fits the hadith?

options.text: Be caring toward the child and respectful toward the elder
Mock the cousin and insult the grandparent
Care only about people your own age
Assume age differences remove everyone's dignity

questions.explanation: The report teaches mercy for younger people and respect for elders. In a family activity, both deserve considerate treatment.

questions.question: Your family prepares soup and wants to share with a neighbor. How can you help appropriately?

options.text: Take hot food outside alone without permission
Ask a parent to arrange a suitable portion and delivery
Demand an expensive present in return
Mock the neighbor for accepting

questions.explanation: This applies the report's lesson of remembering neighbors with food. Let an adult manage permission, safe handling and suitable delivery.

questions.question: One playgroup encourages cheating; another helps you play honestly. Which choice follows the companionship lesson?

options.text: Choose whoever pressures you to cheat most
Decide only by whose shoes cost more
Choose company that encourages honest play
Assume every harmful dare must be obeyed

questions.explanation: Companions can influence choices. Seek good company while treating others respectfully and asking an adult for help with pressure.

questions.question: An elderly parent needs a question repeated. Which response follows the Quran's teaching about speech?

options.text: Mock them for needing to hear it again
Answer with a contemptuous insult
Pretend their dignity no longer matters
Repeat respectfully without scolding

questions.explanation: The verse teaches respectful speech to parents, especially in old age. A patient reply is a familiar way to practice that care.

questions.question: A teacher reads the report about a father giving one child a gift. Which family value should you identify?

options.text: Fairness in how children are treated
Making siblings compete for basic dignity
Believing one child has no worth
Using gifts as permission for cruelty

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ reminded the father to be just to his children. The lesson highlights fairness without asking children to judge their family.

questions.question: With permission, you can give a small amount to a trustworthy charity. Should you dismiss it only because it is modest?

options.text: Yes, only a large gift deserves consideration
No, a suitable small gift can still matter
Yes, kindness depends entirely on being wealthy
No, you must give away every necessary belonging

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages even small charity. Follow your parent's guidance and do not compare your family's means with someone else's.

questions.question: A new child joins a supervised activity. Which small action can show a friendly welcome?

options.text: Make them prove they can buy gifts
Turn away to make them feel unwanted
Greet them kindly and offer a place in the group
Mock their nervousness

questions.explanation: The hadith values small good deeds, including a friendly expression. A kind welcome can help someone feel at ease.

questions.question: A friend privately shares an ordinary, harmless worry. What respects their confidence?

options.text: Post it publicly to gain attention
Use it to embarrass them
Promise to hide any future danger from every adult
Avoid spreading it for entertainment; seek help if safety is involved

questions.explanation: Keeping ordinary confidence shows trustworthiness. If a worry involves harm or safety, involve a trusted adult rather than keeping it secret.
